findings.title: Atomic rename test duplicates integration coverage
findings.why_it_matters: The same direct FileManager failure path now has two nearly identical tests in different suites, so future changes to atomic-save errors or cleanup must update parallel assertions that can drift while adding no distinct integration-level contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep this focused unit case and remove the equivalent direct-FileManager case at tests/integration/persistence.test.ts:160, then rerun the unit and integration suites.
evidence: tests/unit/utils/FileManager.test.ts:70-80 saves an existing atomic.bpmn, injects an fs.rename rejection, asserts a failed save, verifies the previous contents, and verifies that no temporary file remains.
tests/integration/persistence.test.ts:160-174 performs the same setup, injected fs.rename failure, failed-save assertion, previous-content assertion, and directory-cleanup assertion.

The existing integration-suite case constructs and calls FileManager directly; it does not pass through SimpleBpmnEngine or a request handler, so it does not preserve a distinct higher-layer behavior contract.
